source_evidence: In return, the issuer promises to pay you a specified rate of interest during the life of the bond and to repay the principal, also known as face value or par value of the bond, when it "matures," or comes due after a set period of time.
answer: A bond has a set term, or life. During that time, the issuer promises to pay interest at a specified rate, typically on a regular schedule. When the bond reaches maturity—its due date—the issuer promises to repay the principal, also called its face value or par value. These are promises by the issuer; the source notes that an issuer may fail to make interest or principal payments.
